rules.title: The home must remain operable
rules.text: Essential functions MUST retain a simple manual path when Home Assistant, the network, or an integration is unavailable.
rules.rationale: Automation should improve a home, not hold it hostage.
rules.verification: For each essential function, identify the fallback and test it periodically.

rules.title: Prefer local control
rules.text: Local, documented interfaces SHOULD be preferred over cloud-only dependencies, especially for lighting, heating, access, safety, and accessibility.

rules.title: Automate outcomes, not surprises
rules.text: Behaviour MUST be predictable to occupants. Context-aware behaviour needs clear boundaries, sensible defaults, and an obvious override.

rules.title: Complexity must earn its keep
rules.text: Choose the simplest design that meets reliability and usability needs. Every helper, template, dependency, and abstraction creates maintenance cost.

rules.title: Separate concerns
rules.text: Inputs, decision logic, and actions SHOULD be distinguishable. Reusable behaviour belongs in scripts; reusable calculations belong in helpers or template entities.

rules.title: Use stable interfaces
rules.text: Automations MUST depend on stable entity semantics rather than device IDs or transient implementation details when an entity or helper can express the intent.

rules.title: Define ownership
rules.text: Each behaviour MUST have one authoritative owner. Avoid overlapping automations that compete to control the same outcome without an explicit arbitration design.

rules.title: Design for degraded operation
rules.text: Critical flows MUST define what happens when a sensor is unavailable, data is stale, a service call fails, or Home Assistant restarts mid-flow.

rules.title: Minimise hidden coupling
rules.text: Dependencies between packages, helpers, scripts, dashboards, and external systems SHOULD be documented close to the controlling logic.

rules.title: Preserve registry metadata
rules.text: Changes to entities, devices, automations, scripts, areas, or labels MUST preserve intentional area and label assignments unless the approved change explicitly updates that classification.

rules.title: Name by purpose
rules.text: IDs and aliases MUST describe intent, not merely location or implementation. Prefer `bedroom_blackout_close` to `blind_automation_2`.

rules.title: Use consistent identifiers
rules.text: Use lowercase `snake_case` for YAML IDs and helper names. Entity-friendly display names MAY use natural language.

rules.title: Optimise for review
rules.text: Keep YAML explicit, consistently formatted, and locally understandable. Avoid clever templates where a straightforward condition or helper is clearer.

rules.title: Explain the reason
rules.text: Comments SHOULD document constraints, unusual device behaviour, or rationale. Do not narrate syntax that the YAML already makes obvious.

rules.title: Avoid copied constants
rules.text: Values that represent household policy or are reused across behaviours SHOULD live in an appropriately named helper or shared variable.

rules.title: Define trigger semantics
rules.text: Every automation MUST make clear whether it responds to an edge, a sustained state, a schedule, or an event. Restart behaviour and initial state must be considered.

rules.title: Make execution mode deliberate
rules.text: Choose `single`, `restart`, `queued`, or `parallel` based on concurrency semantics; do not accept the default accidentally.

rules.title: Guard unsafe and noisy actions
rules.text: Actions that unlock, open, heat, notify repeatedly, or affect security MUST have explicit preconditions and rate limits where appropriate.

rules.title: Make retries bounded
rules.text: Retries MUST have a limit, delay, and observable failure outcome. Infinite retry loops are forbidden.

rules.title: Preserve user intent
rules.text: Manual intervention SHOULD win for a documented period or until a clear reset condition. An automation must not immediately undo an occupant's action.

rules.title: Use traceable structure
rules.text: Give triggers IDs, use descriptive aliases for branches and actions, and keep traces useful enough to explain why a decision occurred.

rules.title: Design around tasks
rules.text: A dashboard SHOULD prioritise what an occupant needs to understand or do, not expose every available entity.

rules.title: Show state before control
rules.text: Controls MUST communicate the current state, pending transitions, unavailable states, and important consequences.

rules.title: Keep common actions close
rules.text: Frequent actions SHOULD require minimal navigation. Diagnostic and rare controls belong in secondary views.

rules.title: Use consistent visual language
rules.text: The same colour, icon, label, and interaction pattern MUST mean the same thing across dashboards.

rules.title: Build for the actual displays
rules.text: Views MUST be checked at their intended phone, tablet, desktop, or wall-panel sizes. Do not rely on editor preview alone.

rules.title: Use the design system
rules.text: Dashboard changes MUST use the tokens, components, state treatments, and layouts in `handbook/09-visual-design-system.md`; local one-off styling requires a documented reason.

rules.title: Reserve colour for meaning
rules.text: Colour MUST communicate state, severity, or a deliberate accent. Decorative colour must not compete with warnings, active controls, or unavailable states.

rules.title: Keep interaction behaviour consistent
rules.text: Equivalent controls MUST use the same tap, hold, and more-info behaviour. Consequential actions require confirmation or an interaction that makes accidental activation unlikely.

rules.title: Prefer progressive disclosure
rules.text: Primary views SHOULD show current state and frequent actions; detail, history, settings, and diagnostics should be revealed through subviews or more-info rather than shown permanently.

rules.title: Make exceptional states explicit
rules.text: Unknown, unavailable, stale, warning, and critical states MUST be visually distinguishable without relying on colour alone and must not masquerade as a normal off state.

rules.title: Prefer surgical dashboard edits
rules.text: An existing dashboard MUST be changed by the smallest reliable merge. An assistant MUST NOT replace a complete view, section, or card collection when the requested outcome can be achieved by editing the affected objects.

rules.title: Preserve storage-mode properties
rules.text: Dashboard edits MUST preserve `grid_options`, layout metadata, and unknown storage-mode properties unless their removal is an explicit part of the approved change. A serializer's inability to interpret a property is not permission to discard it.

rules.title: Avoid duplicate navigation
rules.text: An assistant MUST inspect existing dashboard, view, kiosk, and browser navigation before adding back, home, or menu controls. Equivalent navigation MUST NOT be duplicated.

rules.title: Never commit secrets
rules.text: Passwords, tokens, private keys, webhook identifiers, precise sensitive locations, and recoverable credentials MUST NOT enter version control.

rules.title: Grant least privilege
rules.text: Accounts, tokens, add-ons, integrations, and network paths MUST receive only the access needed for their function.

rules.title: Treat external input as untrusted
rules.text: Webhook data, MQTT payloads, voice text, calendar content, and AI output MUST be validated before they can trigger consequential actions.

rules.title: Separate networks by trust
rules.text: IoT devices SHOULD be isolated where practical, with explicit routes to required services and no assumed internet access.

rules.title: Review exposure
rules.text: Entities exposed to voice assistants, remote access, or third-party services MUST be intentionally selected and periodically reviewed.

rules.title: Detect stale and unavailable data
rules.text: Important decisions MUST distinguish valid readings from `unknown`, `unavailable`, implausible, or stale values.

rules.title: Make failure visible
rules.text: Failures affecting essential or expected behaviour MUST surface through a proportionate persistent notification, dashboard status, log, or alert.

rules.title: Avoid alert fatigue
rules.text: Notifications SHOULD be actionable, deduplicated, severity-appropriate, and clear about what happened and what the occupant should do.

rules.title: Observe dependencies
rules.text: Critical integrations, batteries, coordinators, storage, backups, and remote endpoints SHOULD have health indicators and documented thresholds.

rules.title: Restore safely
rules.text: After restart or reconnection, logic MUST re-evaluate current reality rather than blindly replaying stale actions.

rules.title: Validate before deployment
rules.text: Configuration MUST pass Home Assistant configuration validation and repository checks before production use.

rules.title: Test boundaries and failure paths
rules.text: Tests or documented verification MUST cover unavailable inputs, threshold edges, restart behaviour, concurrent triggers, and manual overrides where relevant.

rules.title: Make changes reversible
rules.text: Changes SHOULD be small enough to review and revert. Risky changes require a rollback path before deployment.

rules.title: Separate development from production
rules.text: Experimental logic SHOULD be isolated and disabled by default or tested against non-critical entities before controlling the live home.

rules.title: Verify the outcome
rules.text: A successful reload is not proof of correct behaviour. Verify resulting state, traces, logs, notifications, and physical outcome as applicable.

rules.title: Use the narrowest safe reload
rules.text: Deployment MUST use the narrowest supported reload or restart that applies the change. A full Home Assistant Core restart requires a documented reason, impact check, and post-restart verification when a domain or integration reload would suffice.

rules.title: Document operational intent
rules.text: Documentation MUST explain purpose, dependencies, expected behaviour, fallback, and verification for important systems.

rules.title: Keep the handbook authoritative
rules.text: Assistant-specific instruction files MUST be generated from handbook rules. Conflicts are resolved in favour of the handbook.

rules.title: Inspect before editing
rules.text: An AI assistant MUST inspect relevant files, conventions, dependencies, and current state before proposing or applying changes.

rules.title: Never invent entity IDs
rules.text: An assistant MUST obtain entity, device, area, service, and integration identifiers from the actual system or user-provided configuration.

rules.title: State assumptions and risk
rules.text: When facts cannot be verified, an assistant MUST identify assumptions. Consequential or destructive actions require explicit scope and a recovery path.

rules.title: Preserve unrelated work
rules.text: An assistant MUST keep changes focused and must not overwrite, reformat, or remove unrelated user changes.

rules.title: Check references after structural changes
rules.text: After moving, renaming, replacing, or removing an instruction, skill, script, file, entity, or reusable dashboard object, an assistant MUST search for and validate inbound references, discovery pointers, and documented invocation paths.

rules.title: Centralise visual tokens
rules.text: Colours, spacing, radii, typography, and reusable card styling MUST be defined centrally through the theme, dashboard profile, or reusable templates rather than repeated as card-local literals.

rules.title: Prefer native components
rules.text: Native Home Assistant cards and features SHOULD be preferred. Every custom frontend dependency must have a named benefit, documented installation source, fallback impact, and maintenance owner.

rules.title: Follow standard view hierarchy
rules.text: Overview, room, security, and system-status views MUST follow the information hierarchy in this design system unless the consuming repository documents a user-specific reason to differ.

rules.title: Keep density purposeful
rules.text: Dashboards MUST avoid both entity-dump density and decorative empty space. Each visible item needs a task, status, or navigation purpose appropriate to that view.

rules.title: Preserve accessibility
rules.text: Dashboards MUST retain readable contrast, 44 by 44 pixel touch targets, text or icon reinforcement for meaningful colour, and understandable labels for icon-only actions.

rules.title: Define interaction contracts
rules.text: Reusable components MUST document their displayed state and tap, hold, double-tap, confirmation, and navigation behaviour; undefined gestures should do nothing rather than surprise the user.

rules.title: Gather evidence before judging
rules.text: An audit MUST cite the actual repository path and configuration object for every violation; assumptions and unavailable runtime evidence must be labelled explicitly.

rules.title: Separate audit from implementation
rules.text: Reviewing a system MUST NOT silently authorise edits. Findings, proposed remediation, and applied changes are separate stages unless the user explicitly combines them.

rules.title: Report by rule ID
rules.text: Every compliance finding MUST reference an applicable handbook rule ID, severity, evidence, impact, recommendation, validation, and rollback consideration.

rules.title: Remediate in reversible stages
rules.text: Remediation plans MUST prioritise safety and correctness, preserve working behaviour, limit each stage to a reviewable concern, and define success and rollback before implementation.

rules.title: Preserve user-specific intent
rules.text: An agent MUST treat documented accessibility needs, household routines, display constraints, and deliberate exceptions as design inputs rather than normalising them away.

rules.title: Back up active instructions
rules.text: Before an agent changes repository or workspace instructions, it MUST create a restorable backup with original relative paths, filenames, and a manifest. The backup MUST exclude secret values and MUST NOT overwrite an earlier backup.

rules.title: Inventory capabilities, not filenames
rules.text: A migration MUST inventory every substantive capability, restriction, workflow, safety control, skill, script dependency, and authority boundary in the previous active instruction chain. Moving or renaming a file is not evidence that its behaviour was preserved.

rules.title: Keep shared and local authority separate
rules.text: Generated handbook rules MUST provide shared engineering standards. Repository-specific operational knowledge MUST live in a clearly identified local overlay whose authority and conflict policy are documented.

rules.title: Preserve secrets-manager workflows
rules.text: If a project uses an external secrets manager, migration MUST preserve the discoverable workflow for authentication, lookup, creation, update, rotation, naming, and safe handling without copying secret values into instructions, repositories, logs, reports, or chat output.

rules.title: Preserve operational access
rules.text: Migration MUST preserve documented production access, deployment, validation, reload, restart, rollback, infrastructure, container, and repository-boundary procedures unless an authorised decision explicitly retires or replaces them.

rules.title: Prove discovery from every workspace root
rules.text: Every required rule and local capability MUST be demonstrably discoverable when the agent is opened from each supported workspace root. A parent-workspace rule, symlink, pointer, or README mention is insufficient unless the normal agent-loading path is verified.

rules.title: Produce a preservation matrix
rules.text: Before removing or superseding old instructions, the migration MUST map each substantive instruction to preserved verbatim, preserved equivalently, intentionally superseded by named handbook rule IDs, weakened, missing, or undiscoverable.

rules.title: Block unresolved gaps
rules.text: A migration MUST NOT be committed while any instruction is weakened, missing, undiscoverable, ambiguously conflicting, or dependent on an unverified loading path. The stricter rule governs security, production safety, access control, deployment, and destructive actions.

rules.title: Validate skills and supporting assets
rules.text: Migration MUST verify that required skills, helper scripts, templates, documentation, symlink targets, and referenced files still exist and remain invocable through their documented paths.

rules.title: Verify generated instruction integrity
rules.text: Installed generated instructions MUST match the output produced from the recorded handbook revision. Generated files MUST NOT be edited to hold repository-local policy.

rules.title: Preserve unrelated workspace state
rules.text: Rule installation MUST preserve unrelated tracked and untracked work, MUST NOT expose credentials, and MUST report the exact changed files and repository status before approval.

rules.title: Separate installation from system changes
rules.text: Installing or migrating agent instructions MUST NOT implicitly authorise an audit, configuration edit, deployment, commit, push, or pull request. Each later stage requires its own explicit scope or approval.

rules.title: Make installation self-verifying
rules.text: An installed handbook MUST provide a repeatable, non-interactive verification command which exits non-zero when generated instructions drift, required roots or overlays are absent, capabilities lack owners, preservation gaps remain, supporting assets break, or tracked secret-bearing files are detected. A migration MUST pass both the handbook verifier and any repository-local verifier before commit.
